sections.title: Authorization of parameterized sub-queries via _load_query
sections.rationale: The new param_query path reuses get_query_results/_load_query, so the existing org + has_access(view_only) checks are the access-control gate for the newly added parameterized queries.

sections.title: Parameter substitution into query text (injection surface)
sections.rationale: replace_query_parameters and prepare_parameterized_query splice user-supplied param strings directly into SQL text, an injection/authorization-relevant behavior that must be reviewed together.

sections.title: Extraction of param_query references from user query
sections.rationale: extract_query_params parses the attacker/user-controlled query to derive which sub-queries and params are loaded, feeding the authorization and injection paths above.

sections.title: Tests for parameterized query handling
sections.rationale: The new test hunks exercise extract_query_params, prepare_parameterized_query and replace_query_parameters, documenting the intended (and security-relevant) behavior of the param feature.
